head: cb201b4e1d348c90777bdde0b42b94c3538f19a5
summary: I fixed all seven findings; each still held in the tree as reported. HF-002: the row for a folder whose listing failed partway now says "could not be read in full", as the folder tree already did. That uses a new `TopLevelRow.ListedPartway` flag, set by `TopLevelTracker`. The count of such folders inside a row now reads "could not be read (in full)", and the largest-files and kinds captions now say "may be missing" instead of "are not included". HF-004: the unread `_result` field is gone. HF-007/HF-020: a completed scan now clears the results list instead of sorting and binding rows the folder tree immediately replaces, and ShowTopLevel's Completed header branch is gone. HF-012: `FormatSize` and `Count` moved from `MainWindow` into a small `FigureText` class with no WPF, and the `FolderTreeRowText.Size` forwarder is deleted; the row-text classes are now compiled into Core.Tests, where the tree's share and bar get their own tests. HF-018: the report-mode delete-first step now clears a read-only attribute before deleting. HF-019: the window now fits itself to the work area of the monitor it opened on (`MonitorFromWindow` plus `GetMonitorInfo`, in a new `Core/Native/Monitors.cs`) using a pure `WorkAreaFit` function, not the primary monitor's. The full suite passed (389/389), as did the bug catalog I could run and nine window cases on the republished exe. A real report-mode run on C:\ProgramData showed the new captions and the tree header, with the results list cleared.

files.why: HF-002: `TopLevelRow.ListedPartway { get; init; }`. It is an init property like `Revised`, so the 9-argument constructor that SL-063's bug test calls by reflection is unchanged. The Unreadable doc now points to it.

HF-002: `OwnListedPartway` is set when a root child's own listing ends in an error after entries were listed (store.ChildCount > 0, the same test FolderTreeNode.Note uses). It is published only on Unreadable rows.

HF-019: `Monitors.WorkAreaOf(hwnd)` via user32 `MonitorFromWindow(NEAREST)` plus `GetMonitorInfoW`, returning a `WorkArea` record struct. It lives in Native because InteropLivesOnlyInNative allows `LibraryImport` nowhere else in src.

HF-004: `_result` and its two assignments removed. HF-007/HF-020: StartScan passes null to ShowFinalTopLevel for a Completed result, which clears the list; ShowTopLevel's Completed header branch removed. HF-002: both captions go through `UnreadableCaption`. HF-012: `FormatSize` and `Count` removed, now called through `using static FigureText`. HF-019: the height clamp moved from the constructor to OnSourceInitialized, and both the clamp and the move-up use `MonitorWorkArea()` (the monitor's rcWork converted to DIPs through TransformFromDevice) via `WorkAreaFit.Fit`.

HF-002: Unreadable with ListedPartway reads '(could not be read in full)', and the count inside reads 'could not be read (in full)'. The words (TitleOf/FiguresOf, now internal) stay in this file with no WPF, so it can be linked into Core.Tests. `.Revised` is still read only here, as the fitness rule requires. Sizes and counts come from FigureText.
The IValueConverter half of the now-partial TopLevelRowText (Figures, Convert, ConvertBack), unchanged in behaviour. XAML and SL-063's bug test use it exactly as before.
HF-012: the one size and count formatter, moved unchanged from MainWindow. It has no WPF and is linked into Core.Tests.
HF-012: the `Size` forwarder to MainWindow deleted. The class now has no window dependency, and its doc says so.
HF-012: OnDiskText and SizeText call FigureText.FormatSize directly.
HF-019: the pure clamp-and-move-up rule, taking the work area as arguments. It has no WPF and is linked into Core.Tests so it can be fed monitors this PC does not have.
HF-018: `DeleteFirst` clears a read-only attribute on the report and its .tmp before deleting them.

HF-018: the exit contract now says a read-only file is deleted too. It also names the one case nothing can fix: a file another program holds open without sharing delete makes the run exit 3 and stays where it was.
Links FigureText.cs, FolderTreeRowText.cs, TopLevelRowText.cs (the words half only) and WorkAreaFit.cs, the same way StoppingWait, KindRowText and ShareText are already linked.

O-001 / HF-002. A real scan in which one top-level folder is denied its listing and another gets a 995 from Windows at its third listing buffer, fed in through SynchronousIoCancel.OverrideQueryError. Inside a third folder there is one of each. The test checks each row's state, its flag and the exact words.
HF-012: tests the tree's share (midpoints rounded away from zero, 0.0 %) and bar (1 px minimum, the full track) on their own.

O-003 / HF-019. Covers a monitor below the primary, a monitor taller than the primary, a foot below the work area, and a window taller than the work area. A further test runs the real Monitors.WorkAreaOf on the desktop window's handle against SPI_GETWORKAREA.
Fixture interop for the monitor test: GetDesktopWindow, and SystemParametersInfoW(SPI_GETWORKAREA).

O-002 / HF-018: C-008 now also covers a read-only stale report and .tmp (exit 2, both gone) and a report held open without share-delete (exit 3, still there). The expected unreadable captions in B-002, B-003, B-007, Invoke-StoppedEnding and Format-Unreadable (S-001 to S-009) now use the new wording.

obligations.how: TopLevelRowTextTests.AFolderListedPartwayIsNotReadInFullAndOneNeverOpenedIsNotOpened scans a real temporary tree. One top-level folder gets a 995 from Windows at its third listing buffer, so it keeps 1-1999 files. Another is denied its listing. A third holds one of each. Before the fix it failed with Expected "b-big  (could not be read in full)", Actual "b-big  (could not be opened)". After the fix it passes and asserts ListedPartway true/false and the words 'N folders inside could not be read (in full)'.

WindowCases.ps1 C-008 runs the published exe with a read-only stale report and .tmp at the path. Before the fix: exit 3 and the file stayed (FAIL on 'no root, read-only: exit code', expected 2, got 3). After the fix: exit 2 and both files gone. It also shows a report held open without share-delete gives exit 3 and stays, which is the case the WindowReport contract now names.

WorkAreaFitTests.AWindowPlacedOnAMonitorBelowThePrimaryStaysOnIt feeds a work area of 1080-2112 below a 0-1032 primary, with the window at Top 1106 and 860 tall. The window stays at 1106. Measured against the primary's area, as the old code did, it would move up to 172, onto the primary. MainWindow now passes the work area of the monitor the window opened on to WorkAreaFit.Fit. TheWorkAreaOfTheMonitorAWindowIsOnIsReadFromWindows runs the real user32 query. It could not be watched failing against the old code, because that rule was inline in the WPF window. On a real single-monitor launch, B-007's placement check passed ('window 816 px tall at 0, work area 816 px from 0'). No second monitor was available, so the arrangement below the primary was never run on real hardware.

tests.note: All nine passed on the republished exe. C-008: the read-only and held-open shapes. C-001: completed ending, tree header, topLevel absent. B-002, B-003, S-001, S-007: the new caption wording, with layout still fitting at the minimum size. B-007: 'the window lies inside the work area (top 0, 816 px)'. T-001: tree sizes, shares and bars via FigureText.

Real run of the published exe on this machine's own folder. EXIT 0, Completed, 114,292 files and 143,550 folders. TopLevelHeader: 'Largest at the top of C:\ProgramData, by space on disk'. topLevel absent and TopLevelList not in view, so the final list was not bound (HF-007/HF-020). Folder tree visible with 12 full rows. LargestFilesCaption: 'Top 100 of 1,14,292 files scanned. Files in 573 folders that could not be read (in full) may be missing.', and KindsCaption the same. deviations: HF-012: the design's example name SizeText.cs is taken. FolderTreeNode and MainWindow.LargestFileRow both have a member called SizeText, and inside FolderTreeNode `SizeText.FormatSize(...)` would bind to the string property. So the class is FigureText, and the method names FormatSize and Count are kept. MainWindow uses `using static FigureText`, so none of its call sites changed.

HF-002: for the test to reach the row's words, TopLevelRowText is now a partial class. The words stay in TopLevelRowText.cs with no WPF and are linked into Core.Tests; the IValueConverter half moved to TopLevelRowText.Converter.cs. This keeps `.Revised` read only in TopLevelRowText.cs, as the fitness rule requires. ListedPartway is an init property rather than a constructor parameter, because SL-063's bug test builds TopLevelRow by reflection with the 9-argument constructor.

HF-002: the kinds caption held the same false sentence as the largest-files caption ('Files in N unreadable folders are not included'), so both now use one helper. The wording is 'Files in N folders that could not be read (in full) may be missing.' 'Not included' was false for a partial listing, and a folder that could not be opened may have held nothing. It was kept short, and B-002, B-003 and S-001 at the minimum size still pass.

HF-018: I applied the design's first option (clear read-only before deleting) and also narrowed the WindowReport contract. A report another program holds open without sharing delete cannot be deleted by any means, so 'every non-zero exit leaves no file' stays false for that one case; the doc now says so, and C-008 checks it.

HF-019: the design did not say where the MonitorFromWindow/GetMonitorInfo interop goes. The InteropLivesOnlyInNative rule allows it only under src/FsAnalyser.Core/Native, so it sits there next to ShellReveal, the existing App-facing interop, with no System.Windows reference. The constructor's height clamp moved to OnSourceInitialized, because the constructor has no window handle and so no monitor to measure against.

HF-007: with the Completed header branch removed, a timer tick that races the ending can still show a Completed final snapshot. It would then carry the 'before the stop' header until the ending's continuation, a Normal-priority dispatcher item queued ahead of Render, replaces it with the tree. Making RefreshTopLevel skip final snapshots would break SL-063's TheResultsListShowsTheMarkOnATickAndAtTheEnding, which calls RefreshTopLevel with a final snapshot, so I did not make that change.
follow_ups: HF-019 was never run on a real second monitor, and not with mixed DPI, because this PC has one 1920x1080 monitor at 100%. A person with a monitor arranged below the primary should launch the published exe once and confirm it stays on that monitor.

The delete-first step deletes whatever file is at the --report path, and now read-only files too. Nothing restricts it to a report file (the HF-018 finding noted this). A person may want it to refuse to delete a file that is not a schema-1 report.

WindowReport's 'topLevel' section counts Unreadable rows but not how many of them were ListedPartway. A later slice could add a key if a check needs to tell them apart. Schema-1 keys are only ever added.

RefreshTopLevel could ignore final snapshots, leaving them to the ending, to close the tick race described in deviations. That would need SL-063's TheResultsListShowsTheMarkOnATickAndAtTheEnding reworked.
